clue.text: Let it remain the issue — on your head be it!

parts.note: stet is the proofreader's Latin instruction meaning let it stand
issue means offspring, here a son

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off responsibility for a matter, telling another it is their problem to bear.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom 'on your head be it' is read literally: something worn on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: A cowboy hat is worn on the head, so the literal reading of the exclamation describes it.

clue.text: Choose between blue and black all detailed in capital city

indicators.note: each of the three words loses its tail, its final letter
the choosing word sits between the two colour words

parts.note: sky blue, so sky stands for blue
jet is a deep black
to opt is to choose

explanation.surface: Someone choosing between blue and black for every detail of a capital's decor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'between' gives SKYOPTJET; 'all detailed' drops Y, T and T.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital of North Macedonia is a capital city in the Balkans.

clue.text: Show weakness carrying pole under lowest part of bridge

indicators.note: in this down entry the second part sits below the first
in a down entry the end letter of the word bridge is its bottom
the failing holds the pole within it

parts.note: a vice is a moral failing
N is the North pole

explanation.surface: A bridge sags at its lowest point, showing weakness as it carries a pole.
explanation.walkthrough: 'carrying' makes VINCE; it sits 'under' E.
explanation.definitionFit: To evince a feeling is to display or reveal it, so it means to show.

clue.text: Underhand robbing of the electorate at last with the rigged vote

indicators.note: a rigged result is fixed, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: a cross on a ballot paper marks a vote

explanation.surface: Complaint that voters were finally cheated through a fixed ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rigged' rearranges ATLASTTHE; 'with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: A hidden levy that voters do not notice takes their money covertly, an underhand theft from them.

clue.text: Bustle following an upstanding Hebrew prophet

indicators.note: the bustle word comes after the turned word
in a down entry, standing up means reading bottom to top

parts.note: taken as written before being turned
hum means busy activity, as in a hum of bustle

explanation.surface: A righteous prophet of Israel, with bustle trailing behind.
explanation.definitionFit: He is one of the twelve minor prophets of the Old Testament, with his own short book.

clue.text: Great player joining line running backwards before pace cut

indicators.note: the first part is placed ahead of the second
the word for the joining line is written from end to start

parts.note: a seam is the line where two pieces of fabric are joined

indicators.note: the pace word loses its final letter, as if trimmed

parts.note: a trot is a running pace

explanation.surface: A sports commentary: a star player links up a line of attack before slowing down.
explanation.definitionFit: A virtuoso or master musician is a great performer, which the clue calls a great player.

clue.text: Short kind of duck, a d-duck that's sweet

indicators.note: the duck breed loses its final letter

parts.note: the Muscovy is a breed of duck
D followed by O, a duck being a zero score in cricket

explanation.surface: A stammering cook describes a duck dish with a sweet glaze.
explanation.walkthrough: The stammer 'd-duck' splits into D and duck, a nought in cricket, giving O.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrefined dark brown cane sugar is something sweet, used for baking.

clue.text: Highest point lifted as a test

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifting means reading the pieces upwards

parts.note: max is short for maximum, the highest
E is a compass point, east

explanation.surface: Raising a summit as a trial of strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lifted' turns MAXE upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal assessment of knowledge in school is a test of the candidates.

clue.text: Elasticated leotard, one fitted perfectly

indicators.note: a stretchy fabric gets pulled out of shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Fashion copy: a stretchy leotard, an item that fits like a glove.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elasticated' rearranges LEOTARDI.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes made to measure are cut to the wearer, so they fit exactly.

clue.text: European capital lacking leadership over European directive ultimately, one's panned

indicators.note: in a down entry, the first part sits above the next
the capital loses its first letter

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy
a Lett is a Latvian, a European

indicators.note: only the end letter of directive is used

explanation.surface: A beheaded capital and an EU directive, the clue ending on something critics pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'panned' looks like harsh criticism; here it means cooked in a pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Beaten eggs are cooked in a frying pan, so this dish is one that is panned.

clue.text: OBE for tree!

indicators.note: the clue says a word meaning be is substituted for those two letters, since to live is to be

parts.note: the honour's letters read as O plus the verb be

explanation.surface: Reads like a terse award citation, an honour given for services to trees.
explanation.walkthrough: Split OBE as O + BE; swap BE for its synonym LIVE (to be is to live) and the tree appears.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mediterranean evergreen bearing small oily fruit is a familiar tree.

clue.text: Cause of reaction in time has transformed

indicators.note: the letters of the words before it are changed into a new form

explanation.surface: A puzzled note about what something has turned into over time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transformed' rearranges INTIMEHAS.
explanation.definitionFit: The body releases this compound in allergic responses, causing the reaction that antihistamines treat.

clue.text: Old player putting salt on fruit, say?

parts.note: a jack is a sailor, as is an old salt

indicators.note: the fruit's name is heard, not spelt as written

parts.note: a lemon is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: Someone seasoning fruit, with a jokey hint that this might be an elderly sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting on' puts the sailor first. JACK LEMMON was a Hollywood actor, star of the films at 12/25, 14 and 20/18.
explanation.definitionFit: The American film actor died in 2001, so he is a player, i.e. actor, of an earlier era.

clue.text: 11's male priest, boy in the black stuff

indicators.note: the man, priest and boy are put inside the black stuff

parts.note: soot is black residue from fires
Eli is the priest in the Book of Samuel who raised Samuel
Keith is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A man, a priest and a boy end up covered in soot, as in a chimney-sweep scene.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1959 comedy starred the actor at 11 alongside Tony Curtis and Marilyn Monroe, so it is one of his films.

clue.text: Run into gents, bursting, after which brace

indicators.note: the run letter goes inside the scattered letters
the word gents is broken open, its letters scattered

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for run
then means after that

explanation.surface: Someone races into the men's toilets desperate, and then has to steady themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bursting' rearranges GENTS to STENG; 'into' puts R inside, giving STRENG. GENTS is British slang for a men's toilet.
explanation.definitionFit: To brace a structure is to reinforce or make it firmer, giving it extra support.

clue.text: 11's bit of skirt to keep aside in temporary accommodation

indicators.note: the combined piece is placed inside the shelter

parts.note: a tent is shelter put up for a short stay

indicators.note: the edge of the skirt holds the other word inside it

parts.note: the hem is the bottom edge of a skirt
apart means to one side

explanation.surface: Someone's girlfriend is told to stay at a distance in a tent, the 'bit of skirt' slang suggesting a cad.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1960 Billy Wilder film starred the actor at 11, so it is one of his films.

clue.text: Place in Hampshire, wood-fired?

parts.note: alder is a tree and its timber
shot means fired, as a gun

explanation.surface: Asks whether a Hampshire spot is heated with wood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wood-fired' looks like a stove; read it as two words. ALDERSHOT is a Hampshire garrison town, home of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: This town in the southern English county of Hampshire is a place there.

clue.text: Worm found in slipper taken to the cleaners

indicators.note: the worm word is placed inside the slipper word

parts.note: a sled slips over snow
to worm one's way is to wind along

explanation.surface: A worm turns up inside a slipper, which then goes to be cleaned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slipper' looks like footwear; here it means something that slips, a sledge.
explanation.definitionFit: Being taken to the cleaners is an idiom for being cheated out of money.

clue.text: Observer seated in private accommodation with royal couple

parts.note: on means seated upon
loo is British slang for a toilet, a private room
K for king
ER for Elizabeth Regina, the queen

explanation.surface: An observer sits in a private room with the king and queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seated in' is read as sitting on the loo, the British word for toilet. The royal couple is K (king) and ER (Queen).
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator who watches without taking part is a bystander, an observer.

clue.text: See 20
Evil spirits, two capturing new baby

indicators.note: the two numerals hold the other pieces between them

parts.note: II is two in Roman numerals
a cub is a young animal

explanation.surface: A pair of demons seize a newborn, a gothic horror scene.
explanation.definitionFit: These male demons of folklore lie on sleepers, so they are malign spirits.

clue.text: 11's drunk finds woe with a dry season

indicators.note: something drunk is reeling, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A drinker discovers misery during a time without alcohol.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges FINDSWOEADRYSEASON; 'with' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1962 film about alcoholism starred the actor at 11, so it is one of his films.

clue.text: 12's leg gone?

parts.note: gone means there is none, no
on is the leg side in cricket

explanation.surface: Seems to ask whether the film at 12 has lost one of its legs.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' looks like the film at 12 across, but here is the hour twelve o'clock. In cricket the leg side is also called the on side.
explanation.definitionFit: Twelve o'clock in the day is midday, so the number twelve names this time.

clue.text: Hype for US lawyer defending one with unorthodox religious views?

indicators.note: the lawyer stands behind the pagan, backing them up

parts.note: pro means in favour of
a pagan holds beliefs outside the main world religions
DA is a district attorney, an American prosecutor

explanation.surface: An American lawyer is accused of spin while representing a heretic.
explanation.walkthrough: PRO comes from 'for'; DA (district attorney) stands behind PAGAN, 'defending' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Biased promotional material spreading a view is hype in the broad sense of overblown publicity.

clue.text: Build from either the floor or the ceiling?

indicators.text: from either the floor or the ceiling?
indicators.note: in a down entry, read from the bottom or the top the letters stay the same

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A builder wonders whether to start at the floor or the ceiling.
explanation.walkthrough: The down entry reads the same from top and bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect a building or shelf is to construct it, i.e. build it.

clue.text: Outstanding payment for an offence

definitions.meaning: a sum charged as a penalty for wrongdoing

explanation.surface: An unpaid penalty still outstanding.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both excellent and a monetary penalty imposed for breaking a rule.

clue.text: See 12
Some time for us to talk?

indicators.note: the word for belonging to us is spoken, matching a word with a silent h

parts.note: something for us is ours

explanation.surface: An invitation to set aside time for a conversation together.
explanation.definitionFit: Units of sixty minutes are periods of time, so several of them make some time.

clue.text: River first in turquoise, fresh colour returning

indicators.note: the whole string of pieces, in clue order, is read from the end back
only the opening letter of the word turquoise is used

parts.note: fresh means new
red is a colour

explanation.surface: A painter's note about colours: turquoise first, then a fresh shade coming back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' turns TNEWRED, giving DERWENT. The Derwent is a river in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: Several English rivers bear this name, including ones in Derbyshire and Cumbria.

clue.text: Religious leader in power — looking back, no difference

parts.note: P is the physics symbol for power

indicators.note: the word no is read in reverse

parts.note: taken as written before being turned
a tiff is a minor quarrel, a difference of opinion

explanation.surface: A pope in office reflects that things are no different from before.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking back' turns NO into ON.
explanation.definitionFit: The Pope is called the Supreme Pontiff, a high priest or bishop leading the church.
